patch.value: GH-890: extension collision diagnostics omit the effective winner and cannot distinguish safe scoped overlap

GitHub issue #890 reproduces a 17-package workspace where renderer, parser, and preflight registrations collide. Health names contenders but not the effective winner, equal-priority tie-breaking is undocumented, and registration-time diagnostics cannot distinguish safe scoped renderer fallthrough from genuine shadowing. Package authors and agents therefore cannot act on twenty warnings without source inspection.

The SDK defines deterministic priority and tie-break contracts for every override class and publishes them in contracts and package-author docs; Health and package doctor name the effective winner and explain resolution provenance for genuine collisions; Scoped renderer ownership declarations avoid false collision findings while an unscoped shadowing negative control still fails; The full published external package fleet has a documented expected-collision policy and a stable integration fixture
pm-cli 2026.8.3 with 17 published external pm packages installed in one project
Install the package fleet from GitHub issue #890; run pm health --json; inspect extension_renderer_collision, extension_parser_override_collision, and extension_preflight_override_collision warnings
Diagnostics identify deterministic resolution, explicit default priority, and safe scoped overlaps separately from genuine shadowing
Warnings identify contenders only, health becomes not-ok with zero load or activation failures, and agents cannot tell which behavior is active
A normal package-catalog installation trains agents to ignore health warnings or remove compatible packages

value.text: External-fleet evidence 2026-08-04: the isolated npm registry smoke discovered and tested 18 published external packages, all at 2026.8.4, with init, install, deep package doctor, and runtime contracts passing for every package; activation failures=0 and blocking failures=0. The run still surfaces intentional/global override warnings, and pm-graph installation took about 22.8s of a 24.1s smoke while pm-ops completed in 3.9s. This fleet pass does not remove the collision/winner ambiguity reported by GitHub #890; it proves the current packages succeed in isolation, not when composed together.
